title: Field list
summary: A titled description list: term and value pairs as slotted dt and dd, or a data-driven items property, beside each other, stacked or run in; with dividers and a dense mode.

props.name: items
props.description: Data-driven rows, rendered as dt/dd pairs alongside any slotted ones: { label, value, hidden?, href? }[]. value is text only (no HTML); a rich value still uses the slot form. A row with an empty value (null, undefined or '') hides itself unless showEmpty is set; hidden always hides it. href renders value as a link.

props.name: showEmpty
props.description: Shows items rows whose value is empty instead of hiding them (issue #207).

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level exposed to assistive technology.

props.name: layout
props.description: Term beside value, or above it.

slots.description: dt and dd pairs; a dd may hold chips, links or code. Renders alongside any items rows.

parts.name: items
parts.description: The wrapper around the rows rendered from the items property.

parts.name: term
parts.description: A dt rendered from an items row.

parts.name: value
parts.description: A dd rendered from an items row.

parts.name: value-link
parts.description: The link inside a value, when an items row has an href.

cssProperties.name: --pk-field-list-columns
cssProperties.description: The whole column template, for a page that re-flows the list (a flyout on a phone sizes the term to its text; a wide card runs two pairs per line).
cssProperties.default: term column and 2fr; one column on a phone

cssProperties.name: --pk-field-list-gap
cssProperties.description: Row and column gap on a phone.

a11y: A real description list: slotted dt and dd, and rows rendered from items, are exposed as terms and definitions. The heading names the section. Below 640px the pairs stack.
contentStylesNote: Slotted dt and dd are styled from the shadow root with ::slotted (they are direct children). Anything inside them (a code element, an info tip) is light DOM and takes the page styles. Rows from items are shadow-tree dt/dd the element owns and styles directly (parts term/value/value-link); their value is set as text, never parsed as markup.
